ARCHIVE EXCHANGE — Original three load-bearing tensions flagged by Anthony for the cannabis evidence audit (2026-05-18):

1. The pain indication is the one place the ledger genuinely wrenches against itself. NASEM 2017 said “substantial evidence,” the 2026 Cochrane update says no clear evidence, and Wang et al. sits in between with a real-but-small effect. I held all three rather than resolving it, but that’s the spot where a collaborator might legitimately push me to either commit or sharpen the disagreement into something falsifiable.

2. The schizophrenia causality framing — “probable component cause, not provable absent unethical randomization” — is the strongest harm claim in the document and the one most vulnerable to both overstatement and motivated dismissal. I leaned on Bradford Hill rather than asserting causation outright. Worth pressure-testing whether that’s the right epistemic resting place or a hedge.

3. And the entourage effect: I called it hypothesis-not-proof on the strength of the Cooper 2013 double-dummy null and the 2024 PRISMA review. That’s defensible but it’s a relatively thin human-evidence base to hang a negative conclusion on, and it’s the claim most likely to draw substantive disagreement from anyone who knows the in vitro literature.

These three were the explicit load-bearing tensions Anthony wanted collaborative pressure on. They were carried forward into the verification audit and hole-finding work.
